text:
jess: quick sync — we need a small decision for how the console + SDK surface a 'degraded route' vs actual errors. current UX shows a 503 and a long text blob, which is confusing for customers. thoughts?

mike: yeah i've seen support tickets where teams assumed their model was broken when we actually returned a graceful degraded response (lower tier model).

kai: can we stop using 503 for graceful fallback? 503 should be reserved for service-down. maybe introduce a stable 200 with `status_hint` in headers/body for degradations.

sarah: agree on not overloading 503. but also want something the SDK can map to a typed exception so apps can handle it explicitly (not rely on string parsing).

olivia: proposal: keep transport semantics (200/4xx/5xx) for actual failures, and add `X-RW-Route-Status: ok|degraded|throttled|quota_exceeded|fallback` header. SDKs map `degraded` -> DegradedRouteWarning, `throttled`/`quota_exceeded` -> Retryable/QuotaExceeded.

mike: +1. how do we show it on console? a badge on the route page that says "degraded" with a hoverbox that explains cause and suggested action. we should also surface last-24h % degraded in route metrics.

jess: telemetry needs stable enums. please don't invent freeform strings. we'll add `route.status.v1` tag in traces with those exact values. that lets us segment in the dashboard.

kai: what about retries? some degraded cases are safe to retry with fallback disabled. we should include `retry_recommendation: never|client|server` in body or headers.

sarah: hmm prefer header so proxies/observability picks it up earlier: `X-RW-Retry: none|client|server`. default none for degraded.

olivia: UX rollout: expose header + telemetry immediately (server-side), then ship SDK mapping next week, then console badge after SDK is live. run a canary for 10% of requests for two days.

jess: canary plan sounds good. add an opt-in feature flag per-tenant to avoid surprises for enterprise customers.

deploy-bot: deploy started: feature/route-status-headers -> staging (diff: src/route/status_header.go + telemetry tags) :rocket:

mike: quick nit — we must ensure logs don't print the header for PII-tenants. keep header on network layer only.

kai: agree. implement header at edge and strip at upstream if tenant has `strip_route_headers` flag.

sarah: documentation: SDK behavior table + sample mapping. e.g. ````js
// node SDK pseudo
const res = await client.request(...)
if (res.headers['x-rw-route-status'] === 'degraded') {
  // emits warning event, returns 200 to app
}
````

olivia: console copy for badge: "Degraded — traffic served by a compatible lower-capacity model to preserve latency/SLOs." small helper text to explain how to opt out.

jess: final call? do we accept header names and enum set? X-RW-Route-Status: ok|degraded|throttled|quota_exceeded|fallback and X-RW-Retry: none|client|server and telemetry tag `route.status.v1` with same enums.

mike: yes. let's document retention: store per-request tag for 30 days aggregated, per-tenant 90d for billing/replay.

kai: i'll file a short RFC with examples + SDK mapping. assign to eng-platform and eng-runtime for impl.

sarah: +:thumbsup: — i'll draft runbook lines for support: how to triage degraded vs real 5xx.

oj: (in case anyone's skimming) we still return non-200 for true errors (rate-limit, infra down). don't change existing 429/500 semantics.

olivia: thanks all — i'll kick off canary and add console mockups to the design ticket.

jess: awesome, wrapping up. we should announce in #prod-notices once SDKs release.
